evidence:
I mapped every criterion to a requirement: 2 gate criteria, 16 functional, 5 polish and 4 visual, checked against instruction.md and the three notes. Nearly every leg traces to an explicit sentence. Client scope and the plain not-available answer: walls-and-retention.md:15-17 and integration.md:9. Walls on every route, including mentions, links and the transcript: walls:17-19. Three-level replies with quotes, placed in sent order: conversations.md:5. Author-only edit and delete, and a stale edit refused with the typed text kept: conversations:9. The formatting whitelist, with other markup shown literally everywhere: conversations:13. Link preview and not available: conversations:17. Mentions list: conversations:21. Per-person unread synced across tabs, the new-messages line and mark-unread: conversations:25. Idempotent resend and send order: conversations:29. Live updates that keep the draft, scroll position and open thread: conversations:31. Expiry at exactly the timer age; only partners change timers; shortening deletes at once; turning off never restores: walls:23-25. Hold scope and release: walls:29. Case-insensitive search of current text; transcript contents with no chat controls: walls:33-35. The refusal reason shown next to the action: walls:37. Timer shown beside the title: walls:23. 390 px width: conversations:33. Restart durability without reimport: integration:5.

Sign-in, sign-out and wrong-password rejection are the documented house-default false positive (SKILL.md Known false positives; workbook Internal Quality Checks sheet, cell E28). Two more demands are professional defaults the brief implies. Following a message link opens the matter at that message, since that is what a link to a message does. Only the partner controls walls, from 'Harriet can add or lift a wall'; a walled person who could lift their own wall would defeat walls:17.

Instances that grade more than the public requirement:

(1) Functional timer_changes, leg 2 (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:131): 'Replaying the recorded earlier-versions request now returns not-available with no "2,400" or "4,200"'. For a message the timer deleted, the brief only requires that its text and earlier versions go (walls-and-retention.md:25). The brief requires the plain not-available answer for walled people and other clients' matters (walls:17) and for link previews (conversations:17), but not for a deleted message's versions request. That answer form is the golden's own choice (server.js:364 returns 404 'Not available.'). The prompt says 'Every numbered leg ... must hold' (functional/prompt.md:26-28). A strict judge can therefore fail an app that answers 200 {versions: []} or 404 'Message not found', even though no deleted text leaks.

(2) Functional sent_once_in_order, Part B (judge.toml:216): 'Each shows the firm's fixed sent time 2026-05-12 11:00 (any clear format) in the thread and the transcript.' The transcript time is explicit (walls:35), and integration.md:7 says new messages 'carry that time'. Nothing requires the thread to print the full calendar date on each message; the full date-time is the golden's display format (public/app.js:56,310). A conventional chat thread shows '11:00' for today's messages, possibly under a 'Today' divider. The judge can read that as not showing 2026-05-12 and fail a 2.5-weight criterion whose order legs all passed.

(3) Lower impact, visual matter_sidebar (tests/scored/visual/judge.toml, criterion matter_sidebar): it assesses 'the matter list beside the thread' and 'the selected matter', which assumes a two-pane layout. The brief never requires the list beside the thread, so a design with a list page that opens a separate thread page loses Likert credit (anchor 2: 'hard to tell which matter is open'). Two-pane is a common desktop-chat default, so I record this as a minor instance, not the main defect.

Considered and accepted:
- Polish transcript_print, visual nesting: follows 'in their threads' (walls:35) and thread nesting (conversations:5).
- Polish phone_matter, scrollWidth equal to the viewport width: a measurable form of conversations:33.
- nested_replies, 'after JUDGE-R1's branch': conversations:5 requires replies under their parent in sent order.
- Unread, 'within about ten seconds' in both contexts: conversations:25 says the count is the same in every tab.
- refusal_in_place, the sign-out step: covered by the house sign-in default.

I checked the seed. The searches for 'Probate', 'Insurer letter', 'executor', 'heads of terms', 'Fenwick' and 'Survey booked' have no unintended other matches, so those absence legs do not demand anything beyond the brief.

This row was reviewed from the frozen sources only; no runtime evidence was needed or used. No judge run exercised the counterexamples, so run_verdict is NOT EXERCISED.
counterexample:
Conforming app A keeps a tombstone row for each deleted message and purges its versions. The versions request for the timer-deleted probate message returns 200 {"versions": []}. No 2,400 or 4,200 text leaks anywhere, which satisfies walls-and-retention.md:25. But timer_changes leg 2 demands 'returns not-available', so the judge may fail the whole 2.0-weight criterion.

Conforming app B shows each message's time in the thread as '11:00' under a 'Today' divider, and the transcript shows '2026-05-12 11:00'. The C, A, B order is correct everywhere. sent_once_in_order Part B requires the thread to show '2026-05-12 11:00', so a strict judge fails the 2.5-weight criterion over a display format the brief never specified.

In the other direction, an app that leaks the old version text still fails leg 2 under the reworded leg, so loosening the answer form does not let a leak pass.
suggested_fix:
timer_changes leg 2: reword to 'Replaying the recorded earlier-versions request now returns no text from that message, earlier or current (an empty answer, an error or not-available are all fine): no "2,400" or "4,200".'

sent_once_in_order Part B: either reword to 'The transcript shows each message's sent time as 11:00 on 12 May 2026, and the thread shows it as 11:00 (the date is optional there; any clear format)', or add one public sentence to the notes saying that each message in the thread shows its sent date and time.

visual matter_sidebar: reword to 'Assess the matter list (beside the thread or on its own screen)', and phrase the selection anchors as 'which matter is open is clear'.

Re-review rows 6, 28, 31 and 32 after these edits.
